title: Pydantic-first Pedantic Schema: single-source typed estate contracts
owner: Existing IDP schema-conformance and intent-compile owners; Argon protocol verifier for federated transport
terminology: Pedantic Schema is the founder's schema-discipline doctrine. Pydantic v2 is the default Python-owned contract authoring and validation implementation; generated JSON Schema is its immutable portable wire artifact.
existing_authority: Pydantic v2 BaseModel, ConfigDict(strict=True, extra='forbid'), TypeAdapter, model_json_schema (Python-owned contracts only)
principle: One contract owner and one authoritative definition per payload. For NEW Python-owned contracts, author strict Pydantic v2 models, generate versioned JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12), verify equivalent wire validation in every consuming language, and publish digest and compatibility metadata. Do not maintain a second hand-authored schema for the same contract. Non-Python-owned protocols keep their independently established authoritative source with conformance tests against the published wire schema. Migrate legacy interfaces through evidence-based ratchet and canary; no broad freeze.

requirements.rule: One schema owner and contract ID/version/digest per boundary. For Python-owned NEW payloads, Pydantic v2 model is source, generated JSON Schema is the portable artifact; other-language-owned protocols keep their canonical definition. Generated files must match output byte-for-byte. No independent hand-edits or second schema compiler.
requirements.falsifier: Missing authority, unversioned payload, schema drift or duplicate schema owner is rejected/flagged

requirements.rule: At DECODE send versioned generated JSON Schema when the provider supports constrained decoding; independently validate the response via the Pydantic source for Python and a standards-compliant schema validator for JS/Rust. Do not equate syntactic match with substantive truth.
requirements.falsifier: Decoded JSON with unknown/missing fields fails independent validation

requirements.rule: At EXECUTION door use strict Pydantic v2 for new Python-owned typed arguments (strict=True, extra='forbid', explicit required/defaults, types, ranges and enums). Generate and verify the equivalent portable wire schema; non-Python consumers validate the identical canonical published wire shape; no silent coercion.
requirements.falsifier: Undeclared argument, 'abc' for integer, missing required value or raw shell injection refuses before effect

requirements.rule: At REPAIR boundary expose original-invalid result, failed field, attempt, transformed content and validated final digest; distinguish first-pass success, repaired and failed.
requirements.falsifier: Repaired output cannot be counted as pristine/first-pass in Optimus

requirements.rule: Use source-controlled semver and generated schema digest with explicit compatibility tests for producer/consumer and input/output schema modes; flag Pydantic custom validators that cannot be expressed as portable schema and test both languages against shared fixtures.
requirements.falsifier: Producer adds field that strict consumer rejects; CI detects before consumer deploy

requirements.rule: Canonical validators execute from trusted base in the authorised effect door; packet cannot modify validator, source schema or error policy used to judge itself.
requirements.falsifier: Schema swap and validator injection cannot grant permission

requirements.rule: All required execution and evidence envelopes include identity, instruction_id, effect scope, causal parent, source/policy/schema digests, timestamp, tri-state result, proof link and idempotency key. Private payloads remain encrypted/redacted.
requirements.falsifier: Missing source or provenance never yields VERIFIED_YIELD

requirements.rule: Conformance inventory covers the four established envelope families and registered producer-consumer paths. Preserve canonical schema from the existing owner: Pydantic source for Python-owned new contracts, existing Rego/JSON Schema protocol authority where non-Python owned; wire artifact never hand-edited.
requirements.falsifier: A new producer can neither claim compatible nor pass gate with undocumented schema

requirements.rule: Default new Python-owned contracts to strict Pydantic v2 now; keep existing intent-compile and schema-conformance ratchet on legacy corpus; generate no new blanket blocking gate until clean cohort positive/negative canary and rollback. No mass rewrite for its own sake.
requirements.falsifier: Old known violations do not freeze all unrelated legitimate work

requirements.rule: Every schema gate records PASS/FAIL/BLIND including source/version and failing JSON pointer, latency, coverage and mutation test witness; no silent skip.
requirements.falsifier: Disabled validator or empty fixture cannot produce PASS

requirements.rule: For semantic quality (correct business meaning, entailment, safety), supply bounded schema-valid proposals but require independent factual verifier; schema correctness is necessary not sufficient.
requirements.falsifier: Well-formed fabricated financial/domain evidence never certifies verified truth

requirements.rule: Reproducible schema generation: run pinned Pydantic v2 to emit JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, canonicalize output, compare digest against committed artifact, and reject manual divergence; generate TS/Rust types when needed from the wire artifact.
requirements.falsifier: A hand-edited generated schema or changed Pydantic model without regenerated artifact must fail CI.

requirements.rule: Test semantic parity where Pydantic-specific constraints are absent from generated JSON Schema: differential fixture corpus across Python and JS/Rust including strict typing, number coercion, timezone, Decimal, union, null/optional and custom validators.
requirements.falsifier: A value rejected by Pydantic but accepted downstream cannot be certified as cross-language equivalent.

requirements.rule: For new Python/Rust/TypeScript shared JSON commands, choose exactly one authoritative JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 wire artifact; generated native models and independently executed validators must agree on the supported subset.
requirements.falsifier: Same wire payload yields different Rust/Python/TS accept/refuse/unknown-field/null decisions, or schema artifacts have different digests.

requirements.rule: A contract publication must pin schema digest, supported validation dialect, format assertion mode, compiler/tool versions and schema evolution policy. No runtime fetching of unpinned refs into an effect gate.
requirements.falsifier: Replacing schema path with remote URL or changing format mode cannot silently change the admitted command set.

requirements.rule: For binary RPC-only exceptions, require explicit contract owner, .proto+Buf breaking baseline, ProtoJSON compatibility test and semantic validation; do not force legacy agent JSON through binary IDL.
requirements.falsifier: Wire-compatible field rename but ProtoJSON-incompatible name change is detected before rollout.

requirements.rule: Test the exact native/wire semantic gap for monetary values, datetimes/offset, unknown-field handling, numeric limits, discriminator unions, unicode/IDNA, custom validators and schema repair status.
requirements.falsifier: Large integer loses precision in JS or Pydantic coercion differs from Serde and passes without published semantic migration.

acceptance: B1 decoder, B2 door, B3 repair tests anchored to ADR 0042
Actual baseline comparison, strict clean canary and no false denial spike
Cross-runtime schema/policy versions tracked and distributed from existing context compiler
Mutation tests that remove validation or swap schema fail
Live protocol ingress and effect egress show tri-state receipts
explicit_non_goals: No new Pydantic/BAML registry as parallel authority
No schema format that includes payments/secrets in logs
No model treating valid syntax as verified truth
reference_standard: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 for JSON payloads; fit to existing protocols and validators; formal syntax does not imply legal or epistemic correctness

architecture.portable_wire: Generated JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 plus ID/version/digest
architecture.non_python_contract_source: Retain explicitly identified TS/Rust/Rego owner; no Python takeover of non-Python-native protocols
architecture.generator: Existing bin/intent-compile / schema-conformance and contract registry extended; do not fork another gate
architecture.runtime_validation: Trusted ingress/egress validators, with language-appropriate implementations against one canonical artifact
architecture.migration: Current corpus ratchet -> clean cohort -> strict canary -> per-boundary promotion
architecture.rule: No hand-maintained duplicate source of truth

pydantic_pros: Python typing and composable runtime validation
Strict policy can reject coercion and unknown keys
Central model-driven docs and typed application logic
pydantic_cons: Requires Python in Python-owned validation path
Custom model/field validators may not survive as JSON Schema
Pydantic serialization and validation schemas may differ
Forcing Python ownership on Rust/TypeScript/Rego interfaces creates coupling and translation risk
mitigations: Publish generated JSON Schema only; never make cross-language consumers import Python
Differential cross-language contract tests and mutation tests
Pin schema mode, generator and version
Preserve native source owner for non-Python protocols

portable_architecture.decision: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 normative for new shared JSON payloads, not Pydantic as universal language; language-native validators must conform to exact published wire artifacts.
portable_architecture.wire_contract_authority: One approved digested/versioned schema per message boundary. Existing IDP schema/intent and ADR 0042 are starting authority; no parallel registry.
portable_architecture.python_native: Pydantic v2 for Python-owned model implementation; strict extra forbid, strict types and explicit validation/serialization schema mode; output may propose schema but must be diffed against approved artifact.
portable_architecture.rust_native: Serde+Schemars for Rust-owned types; Garde/validator for extra semantics; jsonschema Draft 2020-12 for independent boundary validation; Typify to generate Rust types from published JSON Schema when wire-first.
portable_architecture.typescript_native: Generate compile-time types and use runtime JSON Schema validator configured to agreed dialect and format semantics; never treat TypeScript's static typechecking as runtime validation.
portable_architecture.binary_service_exception: Protocol Buffers + Buf when an explicitly approved low-latency typed RPC/event boundary merits a different wire encoding. Need proto/ProtoJSON compatibility and semantic validation fixtures.
portable_architecture.configuration_exception: Evaluate CUE only for compositional config/constraint tasks; no new global policy engine or automatic conversion to wire.
portable_architecture.http_api: OpenAPI 3.1+ for endpoint operations, referencing the approved JSON Schema dialect rather than duplicating request and response shapes.
portable_architecture.semantic_proof: Schema validation is necessary but not sufficient for evidence authenticity, authority, complete business invariants, truthful claims or causal delivery.
run_time_controls: No dynamic remote $ref resolution on privileged paths
Pin schema file SHA/digest and compiler version
Schema compatibility migration against earlier version
Staged effect-scope rollout, preserve existing ratchet for legacy
